lessons.title: Present Simple vs. Present Continuous
lessons.content_en: The Present Simple is used for habits, routines, and facts (e.g., 'I drink coffee every morning.'). The Present Continuous is for actions happening now or around the current time (e.g., 'I am drinking coffee right now.').

lessons.title: Articles: A/An vs. The
lessons.content_en: Use 'a/an' for general, non-specific nouns (e.g., 'I saw a dog.'). Use 'the' for specific nouns that have already been mentioned or are unique (e.g., 'The dog was friendly.').

lessons.title: Past Simple Tense
lessons.content_en: The Past Simple is used to talk about completed actions in the past. For regular verbs, add '-ed' (e.g., 'walked', 'played'). Many common verbs are irregular (e.g., 'went', 'saw', 'ate'). Example: 'Yesterday, I visited my grandparents.'

lessons.title: Relative Clauses
lessons.content_en: Relative clauses add extra information to a sentence. They are introduced by relative pronouns like 'who', 'which', 'that', 'whose', and 'where'. For example: 'The man who lives next door is a doctor.' Defining clauses give essential information, while non-defining clauses give extra, non-essential information and are separated by commas.

lessons.title: Technology Vocabulary
lessons.content_en: Essential words for discussing technology: innovative, cutting-edge, user-friendly, obsolete, digital native, automation, artificial intelligence. Try using them in sentences about how technology affects society.

lessons.title: Environment Vocabulary
lessons.content_en: Key terms for environmental topics: sustainability, biodiversity, renewable energy, carbon footprint, conservation, pollution, climate change. These are crucial for Writing Task 2 and Speaking Part 3.

lessons.title: Adjectives for Describing Places
lessons.content_en: Expand your descriptions with words like: bustling (busy), tranquil (calm), picturesque (beautiful), historic, modern, vibrant (full of life), deserted (empty).

lessons.title: Education Vocabulary
lessons.content_en: For discussions about education, use words like: curriculum, pedagogy, tertiary education, lifelong learning, rote learning, critical thinking, and standardized testing. Example: 'Some argue that modern pedagogy should focus more on critical thinking than on rote learning.'

lessons.title: Time Management in the Reading Test
lessons.content_en: Do not spend more than 20 minutes on each reading passage. If you are stuck on a question, make an educated guess and move on. You can always come back later if you have time. Skim the questions before reading the passage to know what to look for.

lessons.title: Paraphrasing in Writing Task 2
lessons.content_en: Never copy the question in your introduction. You must paraphrase it using synonyms and different sentence structures. For example, 'Some people believe that...' can be changed to 'It is argued by some that...'. This demonstrates your vocabulary and grammar range.

lessons.title: Extending Your Answers in Speaking Part 3
lessons.content_en: Don't give short answers. Use the 'A.R.E.A.' method: Answer the question directly. Give a Reason for your answer. Provide an Example to support your point. Suggest an Alternative or opposite view. This creates a well-developed, fluent response.

lessons.title: Identifying Keywords in Listening
lessons.content_en: Before the audio starts, quickly read the questions and underline the keywords. These are usually nouns, verbs, or adjectives that contain the main ideas. Listening for these specific words and their synonyms will help you locate the answers more easily.

lessons.title: Hometown
lessons.content_en: Let's talk about your hometown. What kind of place is it? What's the most interesting part of your town? What kind of jobs do the people in your hometown do?

lessons.title: A Memorable Holiday
lessons.content_en: Describe a memorable holiday you have had. You should say: where you went, who you were with, what you did, and explain why it was so memorable for you.

lessons.title: Advertising
lessons.content_en: Let's discuss advertising. What makes an advertisement effective? Do you think advertising manipulates people? What are the rules about advertising to children?

lessons.title: Daily Routine
lessons.content_en: Tell me about your typical daily routine. What is your favorite part of the day? How do you like to relax in the evenings?

lessons.title: A Skill You Learned
lessons.content_en: Describe a skill you learned that you found difficult. You should say: what the skill was, why you decided to learn it, how you learned it, and explain why you found it difficult.
